name: Conduent (2nd Role)
desc:
Remote Healthcare Customer Service Representative (Call Center Representative) | $16.00/hr | Phone Heavy, No Sales Expectations
Company: Conduent
Industry: Insurance Services
What Your Day Will Look Like: You’d answer inbound calls from people with questions about their dental benefits. Callers might be members, dental offices, or employer groups, and they’re asking about things like eligibility, claims, appeals, grievances, or how to find a provider. You’d cover both Commercial and Medicare plans. When someone has a problem, you’d look into it, reach out to the right people, and write down everything you did in the billing system. If it’s a complaint about a bill or a claim, you’d send it to the right department to follow up. You’d also send out plan brochures and provider directories when someone needs them. You’re expected to work through 6 systems and average about 32 calls a day, and your quality and monthly numbers are tracked.
assessment: Yes, expect a customer service assessment and typing test
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: High school diploma, GED, or college degree.
Required Experience: 1 year of face-to-face customer service experience is listed as a requirement. The intro says customer service experience is a plus but not required, so confirm with the recruiter.
Preferred Experience: At least 1 year of call center experience. Experience in the dental, medical, or managed care industry.
Required Skills:
• Effective phone communication and strong written and verbal skills
• Organization, time management, analytical, and problem solving skills
• Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Microsoft Outlook, and Internet Explorer
• Self-motivated, resourceful, detail-oriented, and a team player
• Ability to pass a background check
• A hardwired home internet connection (10 Mbps download and 3 Mbps upload) and a secure, distraction-free workspace
Best Fit
This role is ideal for:
• Someone with a year of face-to-face customer service work, like retail, restaurants, or front desk
• Someone interested in healthcare or insurance who wants to learn benefits and claims
• Someone who likes investigating a problem and following it through to a solution
• Someone comfortable with a structured, tracked schedule and a steady call volume
Not a Good Fit for:
• Anyone without face-to-face customer service experience
• Anyone who can’t keep the workspace clutter free with no pens, paper, or personal electronics, and no one else in the room during work hours
• Anyone who can’t attend all 7 weeks of training, since the posting requires 100% attendance
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process: 1. Application 2. Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you. 3. If assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen. 4. If phone screen passes you can expect the final interview. Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3-15 days on average.
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
• Inbound call handling
• One-call resolution
• Healthcare or insurance customer service
• Claims and appeals support
• Complaint investigation and escalation
• Accurate documentation
• Multi-system navigation
• Meeting call volume and quality goals
• Face-to-face customer service
• Empathy and active listening
4-5 interview questions for this role:
• Tell us about your face-to-face customer service experience and what you liked about it.
• How do you handle a caller who is upset about a bill or a denied claim?
• Walk us through how you’d look into a problem you don’t know the answer to.
• How do you keep accurate notes while you’re talking with someone?
• How do you feel about taking around 30 calls a day and having your quality tracked?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
Pay: $16.00/hr, confirmed in posting.
Shift: Full-time. Hours of operation are Monday through Sunday, 7:30am to 11:00pm EST (6:30am to 10:00pm CST). The specific shift isn’t stated, confirm directly. Training is mandatory and paid, with 5 weeks of classroom and 2 weeks of nesting, and 100% attendance is required. Training hours aren’t stated.
Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision available on the first day of employment. Paid time off starts accruing after 180 days (about 6 months).
Equipment Provided: Provided. Computer, monitor, mouse, keyboard, headset, ethernet cord, and power cables. Participant needs home internet of at least 10 Mbps download and 3 Mbps upload, hardwired to the modem by ethernet. Satellite and wireless internet aren’t acceptable. The workspace must be clutter free and secure, with no one in the room during work hours and no writing utensils or unauthorized electronics.
Felony Friendly?: Not stated. A background check is required.
Drug Test: Not stated.
Notes: Oklahoma isn’t on the not-hiring list (AK, CA, CT, HI, IL, MA, MD, MT, NJ, NY, OR, WA, plus Minneapolis, Washington DC, and the Denver, Boulder, and Edgewater area), but the posting says “including but not limited to,” so confirm with the recruiter. Benefits start on day one, and the paid training is 7 weeks, so participants are well prepared before they take calls on their own. The posting says there are plenty of growth opportunities on the healthcare team. A participant can apply from a public computer at a library if they don’t have one. This is a separate opening from your other Conduent entries.
Career Pathway: Not stated directly in posting, though it mentions growth opportunities within the healthcare team. Reasonable inferred path: Call Center Representative → Senior Representative → Team Lead → Supervisor, though this is an estimate, not confirmed by Conduent directly.
